notes.1: Most candidates attempted this question and apart from a few candidates all managed to give the correct answers.
notes.2: As with Question 1 this question was well answered with few candidates making mistakes.
notes.3: This question was well answered with many candidates achieving at least two of the four marks.
notes.4: Candidates achieved better marks on part (b) rather than part (a).
notes.4a: Candidates were able to achieve a couple of marks for this part of the question but in order to improve the answering of questions similar to this they need to read carefully the question and then give detailed answers.
notes.4b: Most candidates attempted this question. Candidates need to read the question carefully as the question asked for the advantages and disadvantages of going to the bank rather than internet banking. Some candidates misread this and answered the question referring to internet banking.
notes.5: As a whole most candidates achieved well on this question but there were some surprising results. Perhaps candidates thought parts (a) and (b) were harder than they first appeared.
notes.5a: Some candidates mixed up rows and columns giving the wrong answer. Other candidates included all the rows even though row 3 was blank.
notes.5b: As with part (a) there were some surprising results for this straightforward question. All columns contained text apart from column B.
notes.5c: Most candidates were able to achieve at least two marks on this question but surprisingly some candidates missed the question out completely. In order to improve the answering of questions of this type candidates need to plan out the answer and work from left to right as they track through the formula. For example: IF(F4="Y",($I$1*D4*G4),"") would become If F4 is equal to "Y" then multiply I1 by D4 by G4. If F4<>"Y" then display a blank.
notes.5d: This question was generally well answered by most candidates who achieved marks from several different methods.
notes.6a: Many candidates achieved the mark for writing File Transfer Protocol without explaining what it was. Some candidates did not attempt the question.
notes.6b: Most candidates did not answer this question well.
notes.6c: This was better answered than the other parts of the question. The common correct answers were links and buttons. Some candidates gave examples rather than features.
notes.7a: There were a number of candidates that wrote about databases within the database rather than tables. Some candidates did not attempt the question. Those candidates that understood that the tables had to be linked produced good answers.
notes.7b: Many candidates achieved a mark for the primary key being unique. In order for candidates to achieve good marks in this type of question candidates need to give detailed answers.
notes.7c: Most candidates achieved at least a mark for this question. Some candidates repeated the example given in the question and wrote it out in other ways. Other candidates wrote in general terms rather than relating the answer back to dentistry.
notes.7d: Candidates that named a number of security methods produced good answers even though their answers lacked depth.
notes.8: Candidates were able to provide the differences between a hub and a switch but had did not do so well with the similarities.
notes.9: Candidates answered this question well and achieved at least two marks. Parts (a) and (c) were well answered.
notes.10: This question was well answered with many candidates achieving three of the four marks. The first two answers were generally correct by most candidates.
notes.11: As a whole this question was well answered with all candidates attempting the question. In order to improve the marks on questions of this type candidates need to read the question thoroughly before answering it and then give answers with some depth.
notes.11a: Most candidates were able to achieve two of the three marks available for this question. Some candidates missed without permission from their answers therefore not achieving full marks.
notes.11b: This was generally well answered with most candidates achieving at least a mark.
notes.12: This was generally well answered with many candidates able to achieve at least two marks. As with previous questions candidates need to be clear with their answers giving specific technical terms rather than general ones.
notes.13a: Some candidates misread the question and gave the example given. The popular answers were faster to enter the data and saves storage space.
notes.13b: Most candidates were able to achieve a mark for this part of the question realising that they would finish up at the wrong destination.
notes.13c: Many candidates appeared to misread the question by giving inputs, processing and outputs rather than just processing and outputs. As with previous answers the way to improve answers candidates need to give in depth answers.
notes.14: This question was well answered on the whole.
notes.14a: Most candidates answered this question well, although as with some of the other answers in this paper the way to improve their answers candidates need to write more in-depth answers.
notes.14b: This question was well answered by many candidates. The popular answers included ‘microprocessor reads the data’, or ‘speed is output’.
notes.key_messages:
A wide variety of questions were offered to the candidates covering many aspects of ICT theory from simple
hardware identification to the more challenging data security.
It is important that in the examination candidates take some time to read the question thoroughly before
writing an answer. For example, writing that a device is faster achieves no marks but faster to read the data
for example does achieve the mark. Better candidates use specific and detailed language when replying to
‘describe’ and ‘write down the steps’ type questions as well as giving a justification of the statements and
discussing the arguments for and against.
Occasionally candidates may need to expand their answers on to other parts of the examination paper or
onto extra sheets. It is important that if this occurs the candidate clearly writes where the extra part is written.
notes.general_comments:
Most candidates were able to attempt most of the questions and produced a good range of marks. There
was a good correlation between the individual answers and the overall score of the paper. The paper gave
all candidates an opportunity to demonstrate their knowledge and understanding of ICT using a wide variety
of topics. The vast majority of candidates were able to complete the paper in the allotted time, and most were
able to make an attempt at all the questions. Some parts of the examination paper contained new topics or
topics that had not been set for some time.
When a question indicates a specific number of answers, candidates should only write one answer in each
allocated space. Candidates writing extra answers will achieve no credit for these. Any question inviting the
candidate to describe, discuss, explain advantages or disadvantages requires specific points relevant to the
questions asked as well as a detailed answer.
